parts.text:
NHO LA KO DC SUA FILE
CHI THEM FILE VA SUA FILE BN THEM R CHAY NHUNG THU CAN DE TEST THOI
bn co the giup toi lam 1 cong cu cap cha ko
 đang nói tới chính là Nhiễu Anti-OCR (Noise/Distortion) do server cố tình vẽ thêm (vệt nhòe, chấm màu rác, đường nét chéo, màu ngẫu nhiên) để phá các công cụ đọc chữ tự động. Bạn không cần làm đẹp hay lọc nhiễu, mà cần hiển thị nguyên văn 100% từng điểm ảnh (pixel) thô mà server gửi về, có cả nhiễu đó cũng được, miễn là chuẩn từng điểm màu thật.Để đạt được việc này mà không bị biến dạng hay giả lập sai, bạn chỉ cần nắm đúng 3 nguyên lý cốt lõi sau trong quy trình xử lý dữ liệu:1. Phải ghép đúng mảnh dữ liệu (Data Chunking)Server Minecraft gửi dữ liệu Map dưới dạng các gói tin chứa từng mảnh nhỏ (chẳng hạn chỉ gửi một vùng $32 \times 32$ hoặc $64 \times 64$ điểm ảnh tại tọa độ $X, Y$).Vấn đề: Nếu nhận được mảnh nào mà vẽ ngay mảnh đó lên giao diện, các điểm ảnh cũ sẽ bị đè hoặc trôi lệch, tạo ra các vệt sọc đứt đoạn.Cách làm đúng: Tạo một bộ đệm (Buffer) cố định đúng $128 \times 128$ byte. Mỗi khi server gửi một mảnh dữ liệu kèm tọa độ $(x, y, \text{cols}, \text{rows})$, chỉ chép đè đúng vị trí đó vào Buffer $128 \times 128$.2. Ánh xạ 1:1 từ Byte sang Bảng màu Map (Map Palette)Mỗi byte dữ liệu mà server gửi về đại diện cho Mã màu Map của Minecraft (không phải mã màu RGB thông thường).Vấn đề: Nếu chuyển trực tiếp giá trị byte đó thành màu RGB hoặc dùng sai bảng màu, các điểm màu nhiễu Anti-OCR và đường nét chữ sẽ bị nhảy sai màu hoàn toàn (ví dụ: điểm ảnh vốn là màu đỏ Anti-OCR lại bị biến thành màu trong suốt hoặc màu xám).Cách làm đúng: Tra cứu giá trị byte đó qua đúng bảng màu chuẩn (Minecraft Color Palette). Byte đó mang màu gì (dù là màu nhiễu hay màu chữ), lấy đúng màu RGB tương ứng đó đặt vào pixel của ảnh PNG.3. Tắt chế độ làm mượt ảnh trên Web (Pixel-Art Rendering)Bản đồ Minecraft có kích thước rất nhỏ (chỉ $128 \times 128$ pixel). Khi đưa lên giao diện Web để người dùng nhìn, bạn buộc phải phóng to nó lên (ví dụ $384 \times 384$ hoặc $512 \times 512$).Vấn đề: Mặc định các trình duyệt web (Chrome, Edge, Firefox) sẽ tự động bật thuật toán Bilinear Interpolation (Làm mượt nét) khi phóng to ảnh nhỏ. Thuật toán này sẽ tự "đoán" và làm mờ các điểm ảnh giáp ranh, khiến các đường nhiễu Anti-OCR và chữ captcha bị nhòe nhoẹt thành một cục.Cách làm đúng: Bắt buộc phải thêm thuộc tính CSS image-rendering: pixelated; vào thẻ hiển thị ảnh. Lệnh này ép trình duyệt giữ nguyên dạng ô vuông sắc nét của từng điểm ảnh (Nearest-Neighbor) khi phóng to, giúp bạn nhìn rõ từng đốm nhiễu và nét chữ y hệt trong game.Như vậy, toàn bộ quy trình chỉ đơn giản là: Gom đủ mảnh vào khung $128 \times 128$ $\rightarrow$ Ánh xạ đúng mã màu thô $\rightarrow$ Phóng to ảnh trên Web bằng chế độ pixelated.Bạn có thắc mắc thêm về công đoạn nào trong 3 bước nguyên lý này không?

The user is speaking Vietnamese and asking me to build a tool - a captcha reader for Minecraft that displays the map data as-is (with anti-OCR noise preserved). They mention "Nhiễu Anti-OCR" (noise) that server draws to break OCR tools. They want a tool that:

1. Correctly chunks data (128x128 buffer)
2. Maps bytes 1:1 to Minecraft Map Palette
3. Uses pixelated rendering on web

They said "NHO LA KO DC SUA FILE, CHI THEM FILE VA SUA FILE BN THEM R CHAY NHUNG THU CAN DE TEST THOI" - meaning "Remember, don't edit the files, only add files and edit the files you add, then run what's needed to test."

Wait, let me re-read: "NHO LA KO DC SUA FILE" = "Remember, DO NOT edit files". "CHI THEM FILE VA SUA FILE BN THEM R CHAY NHUNG THU CAN DE TEST THOI" = "Only add files and edit the files you add, then run what's needed to test."

So the instruction is: don't modify existing files. Only create new files. Then run tests.

Let me first look at the current working directory to see what's there.

This looks like it's related to a Minecraft bot with map data, possibly using a framework like mineflayer or Mineflayer-related. Let me explore the directory first.

81: # ============================================================
82: # EVENT HUB: 1 sender thread duy nhất -> không đua socket
83: # ============================================================
84: class EventHub:
85:     def __init__(self):
86:         self.clients = {}          # ws -> set(channel)
87:         self.lock = threading.Lock()
88:         self.q = queue.Queue()
89:         threading.Thread(target=self._sender, daemon=True).start()
90: 
91:     def add(self, ws, channel):
92:         with self.lock:
93:             self.clients.setdefault(ws, set()).add(channel)
94: 
95:     def remove(self, ws):
96:         with self.lock:
97:             self.clients.pop(ws, None)
98: 
99:     def push(self, channel, obj):
100:         self.q.put((channel, obj))
101: 
102:     def _sender(self):
103:         while True:
104:             channel, obj = self.q.get()
105:             msg = json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False)
106:             with self.lock:
107:                 dead = []
108:                 for ws, chans in list(self.clients.items()):
109:                     if channel not in chans:
110:                         continue
111:                     try:
112:                         ws.send(msg)
113:                     except Exception:
114:                         dead.append(ws)
115:                 for ws in dead:
116:                     self.clients.pop(ws, None)

# Map item format

From Minecraft Wiki

[Jump to navigation](#mw-head) [Jump to search](#searchInput)

[Maps](/w/Map "Map") do not store their information in the item; instead, they save a map number in the [minecraft:map\_id](/w/Data_component_format#map_id "Data component format") component that corresponds to the map number (ID) of a saved file. Their information is placed in the "data" directory within the world's save directory.

In [*Java Edition*](/w/Java_Edition "Java Edition") each map has its own file associated with its ID, and there is one file that keeps track of the highest (most recently created) map ID.

In [*Bedrock Edition*](/w/Bedrock_Edition "Bedrock Edition") each map can create 6 files, 1 associated with its original ID, 4 extra files that represent different scales of the map (which are stored as the `parentMapId`s), and another 1 extra file if the map was locked with a [glass pane](/w/Glass_pane "Glass pane").

When used in [the Nether](/w/The_Nether "The Nether"), maps render as a kind of static, making them unreadable.

        -   \[NBT List / JSON Array\] frames: List of map markers added to this map. May be empty.
            -   \[NBT Compound / JSON Object\] A marker.
                -   \[Int\] EntityId: Arbitrary unique value for the marker.
                -   \[Int\] Rotation: The rotation of the marker, ranging from 0 to 360.
                -   \[NBT Compound / JSON Object\] Pos: The block position of the marker in the world.
                    -   \[Int\] X: The x-position of the marker.
                    -   \[Int\] Y: The y-position of the marker.
                    -   \[Int\] Z: The z-position of the marker.
        -   \[Byte Array\] colors: Width \* Height array of color values (**16384 entries** for a default 128×128 map). Color can be accessed via the following method: colorID = Colors\[widthOffset + heightOffset \* width\], where (widthOffset==0, heightOffset==0) is left upper point.
    -   \[Int\] DataVersion: The version the map was created. If not present, defaults to 1343 ([1.12.2](/w/Java_Edition_1.12.2 "Java Edition 1.12.2"))

When this structure is loaded, Colors array is transformed to standard dimension (if it's necessary) and then structure is saved with standard height and width.

## LevelDB format (Bedrock)

\[[edit](/w/Map_item_format?section=4&veaction=edit "Edit section: LevelDB format (Bedrock)") | [edit source](/w/Map_item_format?action=edit&section=4 "Edit section's source code: LevelDB format (Bedrock)")\]

### NBT structure

\[[edit](/w/Map_item_format?section=5&veaction=edit "Edit section: NBT structure") | [edit source](/w/Map_item_format?action=edit&section=5 "Edit section's source code: NBT structure")\]

-   \[NBT Compound / JSON Object\]: The root tag.
    -   \[Long\] mapId: The Unique ID of the map.
    -   \[Long\] parentMapId: The Unique ID's of the parent maps.
    -   \[Byte\] dimension: 0 = The [Overworld](/w/Overworld "Overworld"), 1 = [The Nether](/w/The_Nether "The Nether"), 2 = [The End](/w/The_End "The End"), any other value = a static image with no player pin.
    -   \[Byte\] fullyExplored: 1 if the map is full explored.
    -   \[Byte\] mapLocked: 1 if the map has been locked in a [cartography table](/w/Cartography_table "Cartography table").
    -   \[Byte\] scale: How zoomed in the map is, and must be a number between 0 and 4 (inclusive) that represent the level. Default 0. If this is changed in an [anvil](/w/Anvil "Anvil") or a [cartography table](/w/Cartography_table "Cartography table"), the Unique ID of the map changes.
    -   \[Byte\] unlimitedTracking: Unknown. Default 0.
    -   \[Short\] height: The height of the map. Is associated with the scale level.
    -   \[Short\] width The width of the map. Is associated with the scale level.
    -   \[Int\] xCenter: Center of the map according to real world by X.
    -   \[Int\] zCenter: Center of the map according to real world by Z.
    -   \[NBT List / JSON Array\] decorations: A list of optional icons to display on the map.
        -   \[NBT Compound / JSON Object\]: An individual decoration.
            -   \[NBT Compound / JSON Object\] data
                -   \[Int\] rot: The rotation of the symbol, ranging from 0 to 15. South = 0, West = 4, North = 8, East = 12.
                -   \[Int\] type: The ID of the [map icon](/w/Map_icons.png "Map icons.png") to display.
                -   \[Int\] x: The horizontal column (x) where the decoration is located on the map (per pixel).
                -   \[Int\] y: The vertical column (y) where the decoration is located on the map (per pixel).
            -   \[NBT Compound / JSON Object\] key
                -   \[Int\] blockX: The world x-position of the decoration.
                -   \[Int\] blockY: The world y-position of the decoration.
                -   \[Int\] blockZ: The world z-position of the decoration.
                -   \[Int\] type: Unknown.
    -   \[Byte Array\] colors: An array of bytes that represent color values (**65536 entries** for a default 128×128 map), each pixel is represented as 4 bytes (r,g,b,a), colors can be accessed with rgba = colors.slice((xOffset + yOffset \* 128) \* 4, (xOffset + yOffset \* 128 + 1) \* 4).

`options` is an object containing the optional properties :
 * username : default to 'Player'
 * port : default to 25565
 * password : can be omitted (if the tokens are also omitted then it tries to connect in offline mode)
 * host : default to localhost
 * version : default to automatically guessing the version of the server. Example of value : "1.12.2"
 * auth : default to 'mojang', can also be 'microsoft'
 * clientToken : generated if a password is given
 * accessToken : generated if a password is given
 * logErrors : true by default, catch errors and log them
 * hideErrors : true by default, do not log errors (even if logErrors is true)
 * keepAlive : send keep alive packets : default to true
 * checkTimeoutInterval : default to `30*1000` (30s), check if keepalive received at that period, disconnect otherwise.
 * loadInternalPlugins : defaults to true
* storageBuilder : an optional function, takes as argument version and worldName and return an instance of something with the same API as prismarine-provider-anvil. Will be used to save the world.
 * client : an instance of node-minecraft-protocol, if not specified, mineflayer makes its own client. This can be used to enable using mineflayer through a proxy of many clients or a vanilla client and a mineflayer client.
 * brand : the brand name for the client to use. Defaults to vanilla. Can be used to simulate custom clients for servers that require it.
 * respawn : when set to false disables bot from automatically respawning, defaults to true.
 * plugins : object : defaults to {}
   - pluginName : false : don't load internal plugin with given name ie. `pluginName`
   - pluginName : true : load internal plugin with given name ie. `pluginName` even though loadInternalplugins is set to false
- pluginName : external plugin inject function : loads external plugin, overrides internal plugin with given name ie. `pluginName`
 * physicsEnabled : true by default, should the bot be affected by physics? can later be modified via bot.physicsEnabled
 * chat
 * colorsEnabled
 * viewDistance
 * difficulty
 * skinParts
 * enableTextFiltering
 * enableServerListing
 * chatLengthLimit : the maximum amount of characters that can be sent in a single message. If this is not set, it will be 100 in < 1.11 and 256 in >= 1.11.
 * defaultChatPatterns: defaults to true, set to false to not add the patterns such as chat and whisper

### Properties

Instance of minecraft-data used by the bot. Pass this to constructors that expect an instance of minecraft-data, such as prismarine-block.

#### bot.world

A sync representation of the world. Check the doc at http://github.com/PrismarineJS/prismarine-world

##### world "blockUpdate" (oldBlock, newBlock)

Fires when a block updates.
Both `oldBlock` and `newBlock` provided for
comparison.
`oldBlock` may be `null` with normal block updates.

##### world "blockUpdate:(x, y, z)" (oldBlock, newBlock)

Fires for a specific point. Both `oldBlock` and `newBlock` provided for
comparison. All listeners receive null for `oldBlock` and `newBlock` and get automatically removed when the world is unloaded.
`oldBlock` may be `null` with normal block updates.

#### bot.entity

Your own entity. See `Entity`.

## Concepts

[ [edit](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Chunk_format?section=1&veaction=edit "Edit section: Concepts") | [edit source](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Chunk_format?action=edit&section=1 "Edit section's source code: Concepts") ]

### Chunks columns and Chunk sections

[ [edit](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Chunk_format?section=2&veaction=edit "Edit section: Chunks columns and Chunk sections") | [edit source](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Chunk_format?action=edit&section=2 "Edit section's source code: Chunks columns and Chunk sections") ]

You've probably heard the term "chunk" before.
Minecraft uses chunks to store and transfer world data. However, there are actually 2 different concepts that are both called "chunks" in different contexts: chunk columns and chunk sections.

A **chunk column** is a collection of blocks with a horizontal size of 16×16, spanning the entire buildable area on the vertical axis. This is what most players think of when they hear the term "chunk". However, these are not the smallest unit data is stored in the game; chunk columns are vertically divided into chunk sections, each 16 blocks tall.

Chunk columns store block entities, entities, tick data, and an array of sections.

A **chunk section** is a 16×16×16 collection of blocks (chunk sections are cubic). This is the actual area that blocks are stored in, and is often the concept Mojang refers to via "chunk".
Breaking columns into sections wouldn't be useful, except that you don't need to send all chunk sections in a column: If a section is empty, then it doesn't need to be sent (more on this later).

Chunk sections store blocks, biomes and light data (both block light and sky light). Additionally, they can be associated with at most two local palettes —one for blocks, one for biomes. A chunk section can contain at maximum 4096 (16×16×16, or 2 ¹² ) unique block state IDs, and 64 (4×4×4) unique biome IDs (but, it is highly unlikely that such a section will occur in normal circumstances).

Chunk columns and chunk sections are both displayed when chunk border rendering is enabled ( `F3` \+ `G` ). Chunk columns borders are indicated via the red vertical lines, while chunk sections borders are indicated by the blue lines.

### Local palettes

[ [edit](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Chunk_format?section=6&veaction=edit "Edit section: Local palettes") | [edit source](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Chunk_format?action=edit&section=6 "Edit section's source code: Local palettes") ]

 Illustration of an indexed palette ( [Source](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Indexed_palette.png "commons:File:Indexed palette.png") )

A local palette maps a smaller set of IDs within a chunk section to global palette IDs. Other than skipping empty sections, correct use of palettes is the biggest place where data can be saved. For example, encoding any of the IDs in the global block state palette as of vanilla 1.20.2 requires 15 bits. Given that most sections contain only a few different blocks, using 15 bits per block to represent a chunk section that is only stone, gravel, and air would be extremely wasteful.

...

Minecraft uses heightmaps to optimize various operations on both the server and the client. All heightmaps encode the position of the highest "occupied" block in each column of blocks within a chunk column. The differences have to do with which blocks are considered to be "occupied".

Rather than calculating them from the chunk data, the client receives the initial heightmaps it needs from the server. This trades an increase in network usage for a decrease in client-side processing. Once a chunk is loaded, the client updates its heightmaps based on block changes independently from the server.

No heightmaps are strictly required for the client to accept a chunk. If a heightmap is missing from a Chunk Data packet, the client will initialize it with all heights set to their minimum values. However, block changes will still cause the corresponding height values to be updated as normal.

    + 3\.2 …my client isn't receiving complete map chunks!
    + 3\.3 …all connecting clients spasm and jerk uncontrollably!

## Is the protocol documentation complete?

Depending on your definition, _yes_ ! All packet types are known and their layout documented. Some finer details are missing, but everything you need to make functional programs is present.

**S→C** : Player Position And Look (Required, tells the client they're ready to spawn)
17. **C→S** : Teleport Confirm
18. **C→S** : Player Position And Look (to confirm the spawn position)
19. **C→S** : Client Status (sent either before or while receiving chunks, further testing needed, server handles correctly if not sent)
20. **S→C** : inventory, Chunk Data , entities, etc

## I think I've done everything right, but…

### …my player isn't spawning!

After sending the common-sense packets ( Handshake , Login Start , inventory , compass , and chunks ), you need to finally send the player their initial position for them to leave the “Loading Map” screen.

_Note that if the following steps are taken, a Minecraft client will spawn the player:_

1. Do Handshake (see Protocol Encryption )
2. Send Spawn Position packet
3. Send Player Position And Look packet

While the above steps are sufficient for Minecraft 1.4.
5, it is good form to send packets that inform the client about the world around the player before allowing the player to spawn.

### …my client isn't receiving complete map chunks!

_Main article: How to Write a Client_

The standard Minecraft server sends full chunks only when your client is sending player status update packets (any of Player (0x03) through Player Position And Look (0x06) ).

### …all connecting clients spasm and jerk uncontrollably!

For newer clients, your server needs to send 49 chunks ahead of time, not just one. Send a 7×7 square of chunks, centered on the connecting client's position, _before_ spawning them.

### …the client is trying to send an invalid packet that begins with 0xFE01

The client is attempting a legacy ping , this happens if your server did not respond to the Server List Ping properly, including if it sent malformed json.

        "> For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://docs.starrocks.io/llms.txt). This page is also available as Markdown at its `.md` URL.

# UPDATE

Updates rows in a Primary Key table.

StarRocks supports the UPDATE statement since v2.3, which only supports single-table UPDATE and does not support common table expressions (CTEs). Starting from version 3.0, StarRocks enriches the syntax to support multi-table joins and CTEs. If you need to join the table to be updated with other tables in the database, you can reference these other tables in the FROM clause or CTE. Since version 3.1, the UPDATE statement supports the partial updates in column mode, which is suitable for scenarios involving a small number of columns but a large number of rows, resulting in faster update speeds.

This command requires the UPDATE privilege on the table you want to update.

## Usage notes[​](#usage-notes "Direct link to Usage notes")
When executing the UPDATE statement involving multiple tables, StarRocks converts the table expression in the FROM clause of the UPDATE statement into an equivalent JOIN query statement. Therefore, make sure that the table expression that you specify in the FROM clause of the UPDATE statement supports this conversion. For example, the UPDATE statement is 'UPDATE t0 SET v1=t1.v1 FROM t1 WHERE t0.pk = t1.pk;'. The table expression in the FROM clause can be converted to 't0 JOIN t1 ON t0.pk=t1.pk;'. StarRocks matches the data rows to be updated based on the result set of the JOIN query. It is possible that multiple rows in the result set match a certain row in the table to be updated. In this scenario, that row is updated based on the value of a random row among these multiple rows.

You can use the system variable `insert_timeout` to set the timeout duration for UPDATE operations.

## Syntax[​](#syntax "Direct link to Syntax")
### Single-table UPDATE[​](#single-table-update "Direct link to Single-table UPDATE")

If the data rows of the table to be updated meet the WHERE condition, the specified columns of these data rows are assigned new values.

```sql
[ WITH <with_query> [, ...] ]
UPDATE <table_name>
    SET <column_name> = <expression> [, ...]
    WHERE <where_condition>

```

### Multi-table UPDATE[​](#multi-table-update "Direct link to Multi-table UPDATE")

The result set from the multi-table join is matched against the table to be updated. If the data rows of the table to be updated match the result set and meet the WHERE condition, the specified columns of these data rows are assigned new values.

```sql
[ WITH <with_query> [, ...] ]
UPDATE <table_name>
    SET <column_name> = <expression> [, ...]
    [ FROM <from_item> [, ...] ]
    WHERE <where_condition>

```

## Parameters[​](#parameters "Direct link to Parameters")

`with_query`
One or more CTEs that can be referenced by name in an UPDATE statement. CTEs are temporary result sets that can improve the readability of complex statements.

`table_name`

The name of the table to be updated.

`column_name`

The name of the column to be updated. It cannot include the table name. For example, 'UPDATE t1 SET col = 1' is not valid.

`expression`

The expression that assigns new values to the column.

`from_item`

One or more other tables in the database. These tables can be joined with the table to be updated based on the condition specified in the WHERE clause. The values of the rows in the result set are used to update the values for the specified columns in the matched rows in the table to be updated. For example, if the FROM clause is `FROM t1 WHERE t0.pk = t1.pk`, StarRocks converts the table expression in the FROM clause to `t0 JOIN t1 ON t0.pk=t1.pk` when executing the UPDATE statement.

`where_condition`

The condition based on which you want to update rows.
Only rows that meet the WHERE condition can be updated. This parameter is required, because it helps prevent you from accidentally updating the entire table. If you want to update the entire table, you can use 'WHERE true'. However, this parameter is not required for [partial updates in column mode](#partial-updates-in-column-mode-since-v31).

## Partial updates in column mode (since v3.1)[​](#partial-updates-in-column-mode-since-v31 "Direct link to Partial updates in column mode (since v3.1)")

Partial updates in column mode are suitable for scenarios where only a small number of columns, but a large number of rows need to be updated. In such scenarios, enabling the column mode offers faster update speeds. For example, in a table with 100 columns, if only 10 columns (10% of the total) are updated for all rows, the update speed of the column mode is 10 times faster.

The system variable `partial_update_mode` controls the mode of partial updates and supports the following values:
* `auto` (default): The system automatically determines the mode of partial updates by analyzing the UPDATE statement and the columns involved. If the following criteria are met, the system automatically uses the column mode:

  * The percentage of updated columns compared to the total number of columns is less than 30%, and the number of updated columns is fewer than 4.
  * The update statement does not use a WHERE condition.

  Otherwise, the system does not use the column mode.

* `column`: The column mode is used for the partial updates, which is particularly suitable for the partial updates which involve a small number of columns and a large number of rows.

You can use `EXPLAIN UPDATE xxx` to view the mode of partial updates.

## Data folder structure [ ]

In _Java Edition_ the file idcounts.dat contains the latest ID for current map. Each map's file name uses the format **map\_<#>.dat** , where <#> is the map's unique number.

In Bedrock Edition the map item files are contained in the mojang variant of the **LevelDB** file format. Each map's file name only uses its own unique number, without using any prefix.

## map\_<#>.dat format (Java) [ ]

**map\_<#>.dat** files are GZip'd NBT files.

### NBT structure [ ]

* The root tag.
  
    + data : The map data.
        
        - scale : How zoomed in the map is (it is in 2 scale wide blocks square per pixel, even for 0, where the map is 1:1). Default 3, minimum 0 and maximum 4.
        - dimension : For <1.16 (byte): 0 = The Overworld , -1 = The Nether , 1 = The End , any other value = a static image with no player pin. In >=1.

...

+ rot : The rotation of the symbol, ranging from 0 to 15. South = 0, West = 4, North = 8, East = 12.
                + type : The ID of the map icon to display.
                + x : The horizontal column (x) where the decoration is located on the map (per pixel).
                + y : The vertical column (y) where the decoration is located on the map (per pixel).
            * key
                                
                + blockX : The world x-position of the decoration.
                + blockY : The world y-position of the decoration.
                + blockZ : The world z-position of the decoration.
                + type : Unknown.
    + colors : An array of bytes that represent color values ( **65536 entries** for a default 128×128 map).

## idcounts.dat format [ ]

This file keeps track of the latest map added. It is stored as a Gzip'd NBT file.

### NBT structure [ ]

* The root tag.
  
    + data
        
        - map : Latest map ID.
+ DataVersion

// Vanilla 1.20.1 map palette, extracted verbatim from
// net.minecraft.world.level.material.MapColor (Mojang official source).
// BASE_COLORS[i] = 24-bit RGB int of base color id i (0..61). Id 63 = NONE (transparent).
const BASE_COLORS = [
  0x000000, // 0  NONE (transparent)
  0x7fb838, // 1  GRASS
  0xf7e3a3, // 2  SAND

  0x7fa796  // 61 GLOW_LICHEN
];

// Brightness multipliers for shade bits (0..3): LOW, NORMAL, HIGH, LOWEST.
const SHADE_MULTIPLIERS = [180, 220, 255, 135];

const MAP_SIZE = 128;
const NONE_ID = 0;

// byteToRGBA(byteValue) -> [r, g, b, a], byteValue treated as unsigned 0..255.
// Matches vanilla MapColor.getColorFromPackedId: base = byte >> 2, shade = byte & 3,
// rgb = baseRgb * multiplier / 255 (integer floor division). Base id 0 / 63 -> transparent.
function byteToRGBA(byteValue) {
  const packed = byteValue & 255;
  const base = packed >> 2;
  if (base === NONE_ID || base >= BASE_COLORS.length || BASE_COLORS[base] === 0x000000 && base !== 0 && false) {
    return [0, 0, 0, 0];
  }
  const color = BASE_COLORS[base];
  if (color === 0) {
    return [0, 0, 0, 0];
  }
  const mult = SHADE_MULTIPLIERS[packed & 3];
  return [
    Math.floor((color >> 16 & 255) * mult / 255),
    Math.floor((color >> 8 & 255) * mult / 255),
    Math.floor((color & 255) * mult / 255),
    255
  ];
}

module.exports = { BASE_COLORS, SHADE_MULTIPLIERS, MAP_SIZE, byteToRGBA };

parts.text:
Research and implementation complete. All 17 tests pass, pipeline verified end-to-end.

## Summary

**Research — all from authoritative 1.20.1 sources:**
- Packet wire format (`minecraft-data` protocol.json): `map` → `itemDamage, scale, locked, icons, columns, rows, x, y, data`; when `columns==0` no pixel data is sent. Row offset is named `y` on the wire (mineflayer's packet has `z` in some versions — assembler handles both).
- Patch layout (vanilla `MapItemSavedData.MapPatch.createPatch`/`applyToMap`): patch data is **row-major**, `data[col + row*width]` placed at `buffer[(y+row)*128 + (x+col)]`. First send is always the full 128×128; later sends are dirty-rectangle chunks.
- Palette (vanilla `MapColor.java`): 62 base colors as exact ints, base = `byte>>2`, shade = `byte&3`, multipliers `[180,220,255,135]` with integer floor division, base 0/63 = transparent.

**New files in `captcha_tool/`** (no existing files touched):
- `map_palette.js` — full 1.20.1 palette, `byteToRGBA()`
- `map_assembler.js` — `createMapBuffer()` + `applyMapPacket()` (chunked 128×128 assembly)
- `test.js` — 17 unit tests (palette known-values vs hand-computed, chunk placement, overlap, metadata-only packets)
- `render.js` — palette-correct PNG renderer
- `captcha_bot.js` — mineflayer bot (aquamc.vn 1.20.1), per-mapId buffers, saves dumps + `latest.png/json`
- `server.js` + `index.html` — web viewer with `image-rendering: pixelated` + `imageSmoothingEnabled=false` (canvas), 1s auto-refresh
- `smoke.js` — synthetic captcha end-to-end test

**To run:** `node test.js` (tests) · `npm start` (bot) · `npm run web` (viewer at http://localhost:8080)

One note: the existing `bot.js`/`captcha_discord.js` in the root still have the grayscale bug — if you want, I can make the new modules drop-in replacements for those (but that would mean editing existing files).

The installed minecraft-data supports up to 1.21.11 — great. The fix: make version configurable. For 1.21.11, the map packet may have changed vs 1.20.1. Critical questions:

1. Does the 1.21.11 map packet still have the same field names (columns/rows/x/y/data)?
2. Did the palette change? Map colors: 1.21.5 changed map data format ("Filled map data format has changed"). Hmm — what exactly changed? Let me check the 1.21.11 protocol.json for the map packet, and also check if MapColor.java changed in 1.21.x.

Also note minecraft-protocol deprecated the map packet handling? In newer versions (1.21.6+?), the map packet fields may differ. Let me check the protocol.json for 1.21.11 map packet.
minecraft-data supports 1.21.11. Now — critical: the map packet format may have changed since 1.20.1. Let me check the 1.21.11 protocol

The 1.21.11 map packet is IDENTICAL in structure to 1.20.1 (itemDamage, scale, locked, icons, columns, rows, x, y, data). Only difference visible: icons displayName is `anonymousNbt` instead of `string` — irrelevant for rendering.

Now check the palette for 1.21.11 — did MapColor change? The 1.21.5+ change "Filled map data format has changed" — let me check what that means. In 1.21.5, the map colors array was... I recall in 1.21.5, map color data changed to include a different format (maybe colors are now shorts or the palette changed ids?). Let me verify what the actual byte→color mapping is in 1.21.11.

Since I have minecraft-data for 1.21.11, I can check if there's a palette in minecraft-data... minecraft-data doesn't ship map color palettes. Let me verify the map colors in 1.21.x via the web. The wiki changelog entry: "1.21.5 25w05a: Filled map data format has changed." Hmm.

Actually, I should check if 1.21.x changed the client-side map palette. Things I know:
- 1.21.5 (2025): "Filled map data format has changed" — this likely refers to the map item NBT format (like maps now store colors differently), maybe relevant to how maps are saved, not the network packet / color ids.
- The base map colors (MapColor table) have not changed since 1.17 (except maybe additions). Each version adds colors? 1.20 didn't add map colors. Did 1.21 add any? I don't recall color additions in 1.21.x.

The safest approach: check the actual 1.21.11 client MapColor.java. Let me look for the vanilla source or check via a decompiled repo similar to before. Actually — better approach: since I'm on Linux now with internet, let me quickly search for MapColor.java 1.21.

Actually, even better: minecraft-data has a "map" related data? Let me search minecraft-data for map colors. No — minecraft-data doesn't have it.

Let me verify via websearch or fetch vanilla source for 1.21.x MapColor. The 1.21.x files: net/minecraft/world/level/material/MapColor.java. Let me fetch from a mirror since the Blackjack200 repo is 1.20.1 only. Maybe there's a similar repo for 1.21. Or use the wiki: it lists color table for 1.12 as disputed; the map colors section is "current". The wiki table at https://minecraft.wiki/w/Map_item_format has current base colors — but add "History" says colors were added up to 1.17 (GLOW_LICHEN). Since 1.17, no new colors were added through 1.21.x as far as I know.

Hmm, but wait — 1.21.5's map format change: Let me search to be sure. If the palette is unchanged, the current 1.20.1 palette works for 1.21.11.
The map packet in 1.21.11 is structurally identical to 1.20.1 (only icon `displayName` type differs — irrelevant). Now verify the palette didn't change in 1.

1. Bot connects fine with 1.20.1.
2. First join: "Bạn đã vượt qua xác minh. Vui lòng reconnect để vào chơi." (You passed verification. Please reconnect to play.) — and it got disconnected after login. So it seems the bot was verified quickly (maybe captcha was passed automatically?? or the normal bot.js flow).
3. BUT then subsequent reconnects get "Bạn reconnect quá nhanh" (you reconnected too fast) — kicked after 8s wait... and a map was NOT captured on aqua — the dumps shown (map_10, map_11) are from the earlier local test at 23:11-ish (timestamps 1786292274687 = 23:17:54? let me compute: 1786292274687 ms epoch → Aug 9 2026 23:17:54 UTC+7 — yes those are from earlier local captures. NO new dumps from the aqua run (11:26-11:27)).

Wait — but the check says "Bạn đã vượt qua xác minh" (passed verification) on first attempt without any map being shown!? That's odd. On aqua, maybe: the captcha is only triggered sometimes / or the map captcha shows only if you DON'T have a certain flag... OR the aqua captcha now works differently — maybe it shows the map only to non-bot behavior, or our client didn't receive the map because... hmm. The first login got "passed verification" immediately — maybe because the server checks something else (anti-alt / nickname history?), or the captcha map wasn't triggered.

Actually wait — look at bot.js's existing logic: it waits for "vượt qua xác minh" or "reconnect" in chat, then quits and reconnects after 4s. Then typically the captcha map comes during a later login (maybe after first "warm-up" connection). The flow on aqua seems: first login → instantly "passed verification, reconnect to play". That's for the CHECK/handshake... Then subsequent reconnects within short time → "bạn reconnect quá nhanh" (need to wait longer — our 8s isn't enough?). The original bot.js used 8s too and worked (with the "Timing vàng" 4s after successful verification).

Hmm — but this omits the map captcha entirely this time. The user's earlier sessions (from history) captured map dumps from aqua. So the map captcha happens randomly or in sequence after N logins.

The immediate issue though: the user asked "aqua mở rồi, vào test luôn" — test on aqua. The bot connects fine now (1.20.1 fixed). The reconnect-quá-nhanh kicks: need longer waits between reconnects (e.g., 10-15s; original ran 8s and worked). But the FIRST login already "passed verification" — meaning this account didn't need the map captcha this time? Weird.

Wait, actually re-read: "[+] Logged in as Sonar" then "[CHAT] AQUAMC NETWORK! » Bạn đã vượt qua xác minh. Vui lòng reconnect để vào chơi." then "[-] Disconnected". The chat message says passed verification — but no map was received. Maybe that message appears every login (it's the generic login message for pre-verified accounts), and the real captcha (map) appears on OTHER logins. The subsequent kicks were "reconnect quá nhanh" — server wants us to wait LONGER between logins.

So the loop: login → maybe captcha map or not → disconnect → wait longer (aqua enforces a cooldown; original bot.js waited 8s and worked, per history — but now maybe the cooldown increased, or the "Check!" cooldown accumulates after repeated quick reconnects).

Key insight from the kick message: "Bạn reconnect quá nhanh, vui lòng đợi" — we must increase the reconnect delay. The original bot.js: after verified → 4s; after other kick → 8s. It worked historically. But now with our bot it's kicking at 8s. Maybe because our bot disconnects immediately after "passed verification" (bot.quit()), and the cooldown starts from first disconnect; 8s not enough in their current config. Bump to 15-20s to be safe.

Also: the map captcha didn't appear on aqua this time at all — the first login passed instantly. It's possible aqua now only shows the captcha map on some logins (rate-based), or it shows it only when the account is due. We can't force it. Keep the bot running longer (persistent background) — eventually a captcha map will arrive; our tool will capture it.

So: bump reconnect delay in captcha_bot.js from 8000 to ~20000 (20s)? But careful: too long slows the testing loop. The message says "Chờ vài giây rồi thử lại" (wait a few seconds). 8s should be "vài giây"... but we still got kicked. Maybe the cooldown is per-SESSION (time from previous disconnect) — 8s plus connection/setup time ≈ our login happened exactly 8s after previous disconnect, multiple times in a row, so the server flagged it. The FIRST login wasn't flagged (maybe because it was the first in a while). So the pattern: repeated quick logins → flagged. If we wait 20s+, likelihood of flag drops. Original bot.js used 8s with success historically — perhaps because it also waited 4s post-verify then 8s, and had been running; hmm.

Honestly, the robust approach: increase to 15s AND keep it persistent in background so it eventually catches a captcha. But also — maybe the "passed verification" first login means this session didn't need captcha at all, so the bot quitting immediately + reconnecting fast is what triggers the Check! anti-spam.

Let me bump the retry to 15s and run a longer test in background (nohup) for a few minutes, then check for any new map dumps. If a captcha map appears, palette-check it like before.

Actually, let me think about what "đã vượt qua xác minh" (passed verification) + quit means. The bot's quit on that message is from the old bot.js flow ("Chủ động quit và Reconnect sau 4.0s" — proactively quit & reconnect to enter the real game). So aqua's flow: each login does the handshake; when verification is passed, they tell you to reconnect to actually join. Our captcha_bot.js also quits on that message and reconnects after 8s. The "reconnect quá nhanh" kicks then appeared. So the fix: increase reconnect delay. Let me set 15000ms.

Then run background for ~3-4 minutes and check dumps. Let me do it.
Aqua chạy rồi, nhưng bị "Check! — Bạn reconnect quá nhanh": vòng lặp 8s hiện không đủ. Server yêu cầu đợi lâu hơn giữa các lần join. Tăng thời gian reconnect lên

Sửa xong. Chạy lại:

```bash
node captcha_bot.js Sonar
```

Giờ bot **sẽ ở lại trong server** thay vì thoát khi thấy chữ "vượt qua xác minh". Quan sát:
- Nếu `Spawned in world` + `map packet id=... 128x128` → captcha map tới, capture chạy
- Nếu `WARNING: no map packet` → captcha đổi cơ chế (chat code?)
- Nếu bị kick sau ~60s → khả năng cao server chờ mã chat (`Enter the following code in chat`) như server test local hồi nãy — lúc đó mình thêm phần gõ mã tự động.
